questions.question: Which clause filters rows before any grouping happens?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters individual rows before GROUP BY. HAVING filters the groups afterwards.

questions.question: What does SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders return when the table is empty?
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) on an empty table returns a single row containing 0.

questions.question: Which join keeps every row from the left table even without a match?
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows and fills unmatched right columns with NULL.

questions.question: Why does COUNT(column) sometimes return fewer rows than COUNT(*)?
questions.explanation: Aggregate functions ignore NULLs, so a nullable column counts fewer rows than COUNT(*).

questions.question: What does this return: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) FROM staff GROUP BY dept HAVING COUNT(*) > 5?
options: Average salary only for departments with more than five staff
An error, HAVING needs an aggregate in SELECT
questions.explanation: HAVING filters groups after aggregation, so only departments with more than five rows survive.

questions.question: Which index helps this query most: WHERE customer_id = 7 ORDER BY created_at DESC?
questions.explanation: A composite index matching the equality column then the sort column serves both filter and order without a sort step.

questions.question: What is the difference between RANK() and ROW_NUMBER() on tied values?
options: RANK() gives ties the same number and leaves gaps, ROW_NUMBER() never repeats
questions.explanation: RANK() repeats the rank for ties and skips the next values, ROW_NUMBER() always increments.

questions.question: Why can a NOT IN subquery return zero rows unexpectedly?
options: Subqueries cannot be used with NOT IN
If the subquery returns any NULL the comparison is never true
NOT IN only works on primary keys
questions.explanation: A NULL in the list makes every comparison unknown, so the predicate never holds. NOT EXISTS avoids this.

questions.question: What isolation problem does READ COMMITTED still allow?
questions.explanation: READ COMMITTED prevents dirty reads but the same row can change between two reads in one transaction.
